Mr. President, on behalf of Brazil, I thank the Prosecutor for the briefing on the twenty-sixth report regarding Libya. Complementarity remains the cornerstone of the Rome Statute; States bear the primary duty to prosecute, with the ICC acting only when national authorities are unable or unwilling. While Resolution 1970 (2011) recognizes that non-parties have no Statute obligations, Chapter VII mandates full cooperation from Libyan authorities. We welcome the Office of the Prosecutor's strengthened engagement with Libyan national authorities, noting a positive trajectory in this cooperation.

Brazil urges the Prosecutor to provide additional information regarding his four key lines of inquiry to ensure transparency. We must avoid politicization and double standards, ensuring all victims of serious crimes are treated equally regardless of the investigation's status. Although no judgments have been rendered, we appreciate the progress in evidence collection. To foster a culture of justice, we support empowering victims, witnesses, and affected communities both inside and outside Libya.

For this hypothetical workshop exercise, we recommend establishing a protected two-way outreach channel for victims, witnesses, and affected communities within and beyond Libya. This channel is essential to mitigate selectivity risks inherent in narrower outreach and to account for the higher staffing and witness-privacy costs associated with comprehensive, inclusive engagement. We encourage the Prosecutor to further intensify exchanges with civil society and ensure that all serious crimes since 2011 are investigated without bias.<|im_end|>
